page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and text processing. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 688.29 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 61.58 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions support efficient small-model LLM text generation, though performance drops significantly when executing text generation on medium 7B models.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile, the c4n-highcpu-8 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without massive memory footprints. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized choice for stateless compute tasks. It is highly suitable for single-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, text processing, and lightweight web serving. However, memory-intensive databases or large-scale machine learning inference are constrained by the 16 GB memory limit and the absence of hardware acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. It contains 4 physical cores with hyperthreading and a large 260 MB L3 cache, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance, particularly in text processing, bzip3 decompression, and small-model LLM text generation, while multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth remain average. The instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound, stateless workloads that do not require high memory-to-core ratios. It is best suited for software compilation, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight web serving.
